tagline: Up Quartzville Creek, where a gold pan still counts as gear.
intro: Five miles east of Sweet Home, Quartzville Road turns off US 20, and before long it has Quartzville Creek alongside, keeping to the creek's right bank on the way up toward the Cascades. Twelve miles of the creek below the national forest line are a designated Wild and Scenic river.

The creek takes its name from Quartzville, a former townsite up a side gulch. The gold has not quite been given up on. Recreational mining is allowed along the BLM stretch, and people still come to pan the creek.

moments.title: Cascade Falls
moments.text: At the Dogwood Recreation Site a waterfall comes down a small side stream into Quartzville Creek, and it is known as a point for rafting the corridor.

moments.title: Yellowbottom
moments.text: Where Yellowbottom Creek comes in, the campground is closed to camping now, but the swimming area on the creek is still open.
